conventions.convention: The wave operator is ∂t²−c²Δ with c>0. Classical slab solutions are C² at positive times; Cauchy data are pointwise limits of u and u_t. Unit-speed rescaling sends the velocity datum to u1/c.
Spherical means divide by ω(n−1)=nVn. For even n, Wf(x,r) is the weighted ball integral divided by n!!Vn. Sphere and weighted-ball integration assume Countable Choice.
Spherical means have an even Ck signed-radius extension; available odd radial derivatives vanish at zero.
Duhamel's principle requires jointly continuous spatial derivatives through floor(n/2)+1, but requires no time derivatives of the source and no common compact support for its slices.
Energy density is (u_t²+c²|Du|²)/2 and outward energy flux is q=−c²u_tDu.
A backward frustum has lateral outward normal (radial unit vector,c)/sqrt(1+c²). Its area factor cancels the normal denominator, leaving lateral flux c[(u_t−c∂ru)²+c²|Dtan u|²]/2.
Whole-space energy uniqueness assumes finite initial energy and sharp conservation E(t)=E(0); conservation only on the open time interval does not by itself identify the initial energy.

Strong Huygens means invariance under admissible data changes vanishing on a neighbourhood of the sphere. Bare equality of data values on the sphere does not preserve the transverse derivatives used by odd-dimensional formulas.

BMO uses complex locally integrable functions and all nondegenerate axis-parallel cubes. Its seminorm uses oscillation about the cube mean; the quotient identifies almost-everywhere differences by complex constants.
Stopping uses dyadic cubes of all integer generations. A stopping parent differs from the immediate dyadic parent; the latter is contained in the stopping parent.
The H¹ kernel is fixed, and auxiliary grand-maximal orders retain the supplier's kernel-dependent threshold. L² atoms satisfy ||a||2≤|Q|^(−1/2), support in Q, and zero mean.

H¹–BMO tests are bilinear integrals ∫fb. Hilbert Riesz representation uses the first-variable-linear inner product ∫f conjugate(g), so the bilinear local representative is the conjugate of the Riesz vector.
The general BMO functional construction and duality assume full Choice, supplying the ultrafilter lemma and a weak-star cluster point; a convergent subsequence is not asserted.

The recorded two-grid comparison is on the circle and requires d(δ)>0. Mere non-dyadicity is insufficient. Checked against [Mei, Theorem 2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0304417); the separate signed-logarithm line witness agrees with [Kinnunen, Examples 3.5(3)–(4)](https://math.aalto.fi/~jkkinnun/files/harmonic_analysis.pdf).

The lacunary example concerns finite coefficient support and frequencies a2^n≤|ξn|≤b2^n; constants retain a,b and the adapted bump. This matches the finite-sum scope of [Tao, Exercise Q4](https://www.math.ucla.edu/~tao/247a.1.06f/notes4.pdf).

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, for n≥1, k≥1 and f∈Ck(Rn), spherical means are Ck with derivatives obtained under the integral, have the stated locally uniform zero-radius limits, and admit an even Ck signed-radius extension; |∂rMf(x,r)|≤sup over Br(x) of |Df|.

Assume Countable Choice. For n=2k+1≥3, c>0, u0∈C^(k+2)(Rn), u1∈C^(k+1)(Rn) and Dt=t^(−1)∂t, u=[∂t Dt^(k−1)(t^(n−2)Mu0(x,ct))+Dt^(k−1)(t^(n−2)Mu1(x,ct))]/(n−2)!! is C² for positive times and solves u_tt=c²Δu; n=3 gives Kirchhoff's formula.
Assume Countable Choice. For n=2k≥2, c>0, u0∈C^(k+2)(Rn), u1∈C^(k+1)(Rn), u=c^(1−n)[∂t Dt^(k−1)Wu0(x,ct)+Dt^(k−1)Wu1(x,ct)] is C² for positive times and solves u_tt=c²Δu; n=2 gives Poisson's formula.

Under Countable Choice, for the stated frustum and a C² solution near its closure, ∫K f u_t=E(t2)−E(t1)+∫t1^t2∫sphere ℓ, where ℓ=ce−c²u_t∂ru=c[(u_t−c∂ru)²+c²|Dtan u|²]/2≥0. Homogeneous cone energy is nonincreasing.

Assume Countable Choice. If a C² solution exists on a neighbourhood of the closed backward cone, its source vanishes on the cone and both Cauchy data vanish on the open base ball, then the solution vanishes on the whole closed cone, including its vertex.
For b∈BMO(Rn) and a cube-supported (1,∞,0)-atom a, ∫ab converges absolutely and |∫ab|≤||b||BMO, independently of a and its supporting cube.

Under Countable Choice, an L²-bounded Calderon–Zygmund operator with the stated off-support representation and a standard δ-Hölder kernel defines a linear localisation class Tb∈BMO/C for every b∈L∞. The tails converge absolutely, nested localisations differ by constants, ||Tb||BMO≤C(n,δ)(A2′+B)||b||∞, and the class agrees with the L² action when b also belongs to L².

Assume Countable Choice. There are positive dimensional constants cn,Cn such that for every b∈BMO(Rn), cube Q and λ>0, |{x∈Q:|b(x)−bQ|>λ}|≤Cn|Q|exp(−cnλ/||b||BMO). At zero seminorm the left side is interpreted as zero.
Under Countable Choice and the fixed kernel and auxiliary order, every cube-supported L² function f with zero mean lies in H¹ and satisfies ||f||H¹≤C(n,Ñ,φ)|Q|^(1/2)||f||2.

Under Countable Choice and the fixed kernel and auxiliary order, every bounded H¹ functional has unique mean-zero local L² representatives uQ satisfying Λ(f)=∫Q uQ f. Nested representatives differ by constants on the smaller cube and glue to a locally integrable u, unique modulo constants.

Assume Choice and the fixed H¹ parameters. Every b∈BMO has a unique bounded functional Λb with Λb(a)=∫ab on every H¹ atom and ||Λb||≤C(n,Ñ,φ)||b||BMO. The map is linear, annihilates constants, factors through BMO/C and equals ∫gb on finite atomic sums.

Assume Choice and the fixed H¹ kernel and auxiliary order. The map BMO(Rn)/C→(H¹(Rn))* sending b to Λb is a linear bijection with c||b||BMO≤||Λb||≤C||b||BMO, for positive finite constants depending on the stated parameters.

concerns.concern: For n=1 the Statement allows 'a bounded open interval' without nonemptiness. The opened def-interval permits empty open intervals, whereas Proof 3.1 asserts 'U is nonempty, bounded and open, so ∂U≠∅' and selects a boundary point. The empty-domain conclusion is trivially true, but that case needs an initial split or an explicit nondegeneracy hypothesis.

alerts.finding: The Statement says 'At the upper endpoint the natural dual scale is BMO modulo constants ... by the duality' and cites thm-real-hone-bmo-duality. It names the scale without explicitly stating the supplied linear bijection BMO(Rn)/C→(H¹(Rn))* with equivalent norms. Full Choice is correctly inherited and no mathematical overclaim was identified; the omission falls short of this task's explicit proposition-level seam requirement.
